title: John Casme's band, Manny Gabriel and giving away Elks jobs
summary: He recounts a quarrel with sideman Manny Gabriel in John's band, and giving Elks parades to John and Red who then took work behind his back.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: I remember you told me once about how they-

Yeah, man, that old boy Manny, or what it was, Manny Gabriel, he come in there, he ogden, he. Poor Joe Nicholas without disturbing him, poor Joe Nicholas. He want to come talk with Joe Nicholas and Joe, with Joe Nicholas. That man could, who? That man should play parade by himself. That's why they call him Wooden Joe. So, he's got about three or four trumpets. He break the line and go up there and tell the fella what then told Joe Nicholas, what he ain't doing. And buoy me up, you know what I mean? So, I told him, I said, listen, I wouldn't tell him nothing that day. So, we had to play a funeral parade in something over the river for the young men over the river there, you know? So, when I came there, all the boys was sitting on the porch, you know? On the gallery there by the hall, you see? So, first man I seen Manny Gabriel, I got mad. Soon, angry, you know, soon I seen him, you know? Because I know it's going to be some more, but you know what I mean? So, finally, well, soon I got up there, I started to go back, you know? Remus said, no, don't do that. You know what I mean? So, he said, I said, you here back, you back here again? I said, let me tell you something. I said, of course, I said, listen, this band is not my band. I said, John is the manager of this band. I said, but I'm going to tell you. I said, you know what I told him to be? I said, look, don't get the wrong idea that I'm trying to take advantage of you because you're on my side of the river. He said, I'll tell you that on your side, you know? I said, look, you're going to play the saxophone today or else if you don't play at all. I said, and you're going to stop going, stopping the fellas from playing. I said, and the fellas working and you not working. I said, you know what's going to happen? I said, suppose everybody just take down. I said, what the music going to be at then? I said, that'd be rotten. You know what I mean? It's all right. He played that day. He ain't all good. So, John fired him. John got rid of him. I told him, I said, George, I said, that fella going to mess you up with his time. I said, everybody going to walk off the street and leave you standing there with your clown. So, John fired him. John fired him. He did all right. John wanted us to play. So, this other boy to play trombone with John. Tom Babel's son. He used to play trombone with John. So, them fellas, I used to get parades over there for my organization. The Elks. Now, I belong to the Elks. And anything, you know what I mean? Like, anything like that, I'm supposed to get it, you know. Who should never would belong to the Elks. I'll get the job. I didn't ever want it, you know. Boy, a friend of mine, he used to keep books there, you know. Every time they'd have parades or something. He'd say, well, kid, I got a job coming up here. He said, if you want it, you can have it, you know what I mean? So, I used to get a job and give it to John. So, this boy over there, he call himself double-crossed, call himself double-crossed. Him and John, they went behind my back and they start taking the job, get the job from the people itself. So, I told him, I said, listen, I said, y'all, I said, listen, look, y'all not hurting me. I said, I'll get the job to help y'all. I said, I don't fool no parade. I don't have no brass band. You know what I mean? Just like that, you know. All they thought they was doing wonderful, you know what I mean? Doing me that trick, you know. They wasn't doing me nothing. Look, Mr. Bill, I wasn't getting nothing out of that.
You wasn't getting nothing out of that.

Now, the thing, I wasn't getting nothing out of it. Because most, look, most of all the money, when I do get a job, the fellas ask me, John, or her, already like me. They say, well, kid, say you got a job. You going to wait? I said, man, I ain't particular, but well, I said, y'all is the one got the brass band. You know what I mean? Oh, no, we want you to wait. You know what I mean? I wasn't particular. Well, I just get it to them. But you know what a lot of people used to tell me? Man, you're nothing but a fool get jobs and give them fellas. That's why people used to tell me that.
You could have gotten the leader's pay anyway.

You know what I used to do? If I get leader pay, I pay to the leader in the band. That's right. See? So, Red, I wouldn't give Red no more job, because Red used to like to auger him, you see? So, I quit giving him the job, but I used to give it to John.
You told me once when he wouldn't walk, he sat down. Yeah, he sat down.

I told him, I said, Red, I said, this your band. I said, it's not my band. He wouldn't go. And Remus, that's the time Remus got angry. You know? Remus said, I'm going to stop fooling these fellas. He said, man, these fellas, they got their band and they hired a player with them and then they don't want to work. You know what I mean? I said, you were right about that. So, well, when I get jobs like that, they always want me to work. You know what I mean? But I wasn't particularly, you know what I mean? I just get it to help them, you know? But if I listen to other people, you know what I mean? I just let the job slide, you know what I mean? Let people get somebody else. So, a lot of times I do that, well, I take the load off the organization, you know? Well, they leave it up to me. Well, they don't have no more worry. I'm going to worry. Yeah. So, well, I do it and I just show them I wasn't like them, you know what I mean? But Mr. Bill, in fact, them fellas never gave me no job. Since we've been having the band, they never gave me a job.
None of them bands. You know what they do?
